research_inputs.finding: Outcome-Aware Tool Selection separates offline outcome refinement from a low-latency CPU serving path and warns that learned rerankers can hurt with sparse data.
research_inputs.used_for: bounded caller-observed feedback and no-LLM-in-routing-path design

research_inputs.finding: Agent systems require explicit policy, memory, planners, tool routers, verifiers, trace-first evaluation, and bounded side effects.
research_inputs.used_for: verification, traceability, and keeping feedback separate from authority

research_inputs.finding: Production gateway patterns include cooldowns, fallbacks, health-check routing, budgets, adaptive routing, and request prioritization.
research_inputs.used_for: circuit-breaker cooldown, fallback, and adaptive score design

research_inputs.finding: vLLM documents model-aware and prefix-aware routing, multimodel serving, observability, and KV-cache offloading.

limitations: Outcome records are caller-observed control-plane data and are not independently attested truth.
The adaptive score is bounded request-class feedback, not model retraining or autonomous privileged-code modification.
Cooldowns are local in-process circuit-breaker state; distributed quorum synchronization is out of scope.
Benchmarks measure local routing overhead only, not model quality, tokens per second, network performance, accelerator utilization, or production cost.
No external provider call, model inference, browser action, robotics action, GPU/NPU test, or physical qualification was performed.
This evidence does not claim AGI, learning of a foundation model, model superiority, or production approval.
